original_value: AbstractThe software developers and researchers have been facing difficulties regarding software development effort estimation (SDEE) since 1960s. Both overestimation and underestimation are problematic for future software development. The software engineering field is continuously adapting new technologies and development methodologies, so there is always a requirement to have an accurate SDEE method that can cater the needs of continually growing software industry. The major purpose of this state‐of‐the‐art review is to provide an additional insight of existing SDEE studies while considering five points of reference: techniques used to construct models, strengths and weaknesses of different models, availability of benchmark data sets, data set characteristics, generalization ability of models. We have performed a comprehensive review of SDEE studies published in the period 1981‐2016. We have defined a new scheme of categorizing existing SDEE models. We have found that a majority of available data sets do not include complete information of projects, which misleads the direction of research. To compare SDEE models, we recommend to use same data sets while focusing on specific aspects of accuracy as none of SDEE studies has yet been able to compare all the existing models over same data sets while considering same aspects of accuracy.

result.paraphrase: Since the 1960s, software developers and researchers have struggled with software development effort estimation (SDEE). Both overestimation and underestimation can harm future software development. Because software engineering is continually adopting new technologies and development methodologies, there is an ongoing need for accurate SDEE methods that can meet the demands of a growing software industry. This state-of-the-art review aims to add insight into existing SDEE studies through five reference points: model-construction techniques, the strengths and weaknesses of different models, the availability of benchmark datasets, dataset characteristics, and model generalization ability. We conducted a comprehensive review of SDEE studies published from 1981 to 2016. We also introduced a new scheme for categorizing existing SDEE models. We found that most available datasets lack complete project information, which misdirects research. For comparing SDEE models, we recommend using the same datasets while concentrating on specific aspects of accuracy, since no SDEE study has yet compared all existing models on the same datasets while evaluating the same accuracy aspects.
